display.title: Episode 272: The Vanishing Bottle of Wine (Pesach)
display.summary_short: One week before Pesach: freedom of body and soul, a teacher's taped thank-you for the children's prayers, Shema with a Beis Yaakov class, and how a dream saved a town from a blood libel.
display.summary_long: Broadcast one week before Pesach 5747. Uncle Yossi explains that the Exodus freed our bodies, while receiving the Torah forty-nine days later freed our souls, and that the final Geulah will be complete for both. After the Hakochainik march to a Pesach tune and a sponsor message, he announces the Tzivos Hashem Chol HaMoed Pesach fair. He then shares good news: a teacher in Australia, for whom listeners prayed, has fully recovered, and her taped message thanks the children, saying Hashem always listens to children's Tehillim. A third-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school recites the Shema. Story time, for Pesach: Reb Arele, a devoted shul shamash, dreams three times that a voice asks, 'Where is the wine for Pesach?' He finds that the wine bottle kept in the Aron Kodesh has been swapped for blood by a wicked man plotting a blood libel, and replaces it. When the villain brings the king on Pesach, the bottle holds only wine and the plotter gives himself away. The show closes with Seder dates, selling chametz and Pesach greetings.
display.lesson: Hashem, the Guardian of Israel, never slumbers; He protects us in every generation, and the prayers of children go straight to Him.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: 'exactly one week before Pesach'; Seders Monday and Tuesday nights, April 13 and 14.

advisories.note: A blood libel plot: a villain plants a bottle of blood in the shul's ark to accuse the Jews before the king; it is foiled by a miracle.

sources_cited.note: 'He does not slumber nor sleep, the Guardian of Israel.'
In every generation they rise against us, and Hashem saves us.
